title_clean: How Your Broker Is Stealing Your Money (5 Methods)
summary: Five broker-cheating methods from personal experience: inflated 'transaction charges' masking brokerage, illegal interest on collateral, per-share-vs-per-lot 'computer mistakes' (₹60,000 charged on two lots), percentage pledging fees vs CDSL's ₹5, and uncredited pay-in cheques.
lessons: Judge brokers by total cost per lot including transaction charges, never headline brokerage.
No interest can be charged on F&O collateral - it is an agreement settled by exchange margins, not a loan.
Check contract notes: a 'per lot' brokerage charged 'per share' multiplies by lot size.
Pledging should cost the CDSL rate (about ₹5-10), never a percentage of value.
Reconcile every pay-in against the ledger; cheques can be banked without being credited.

title_clean: Broker Scams Part 2: Stamp Duty, Square-Off Algorithms and Margin Double-Blocking
summary: Three more broker abuses: collecting Tamil Nadu's stayed ₹600/cr stamp duty while courts held it at ₹50/cr (pocketing ₹550/cr), a low-cost broker squaring off all 5 lots over a ₹25,000 shortfall, and brokers double-blocking option premium on top of NSE's integrated margin display.
lessons: A court-stayed charge can still be collected at the headline rate - demand proof of what was actually paid to the government.
Square-off algorithms may liquidate entire positions when squaring one lot would restore the required buffer.
After NSE integrated premium into displayed margin, most brokers still block premium again on top - locking trader capital.
The rise of a flat-fee disruptive broker in a decade shows how badly incumbents served clients.

title_clean: How Trainers and Traders Lure You: Workshop Scams and Fake P&L

lessons: Price training as a percentage of capital: 2% is reasonable, 50% (fee plus forced software) is ruinous.

title_clean: How Bond Prices Work: Yield vs Interest, Market-Rate Mechanics
summary: Bond pricing via a non-callable FD analogy: accreted interest raises fair value over time; when market rates rise, existing bonds trade cheaper (yield up); when rates fall, they trade at premium (yield down). Live examples: Bharat Bond 2030 at ₹1,108 premium, 2031 at discount.
lessons: A cumulative bond's fair value grows by accreted interest; early exit means accepting the market price.
Rising economy-wide rates push existing bond prices down and yields up; falling rates do the opposite.
Coupon is fixed on face value; yield is what the current price implies - they diverge as price moves.
Bond math is the transmission channel from central-bank policy to equity valuations.

title_clean: Bonds, Interest Rates and the Stock Market: The Two-Sided Coin
summary: Why rising rates can coexist with roaring bulls: 2003-07 Sensex went ~3,000 to ~21,000 while RBI hiked at every policy. Rate mechanics: cuts stimulate spending and reviving economies; hikes cool inflation. Fear in Feb-2021 came from the pace and source of the US-yield rise, not the level.
lessons: Rising rates often signal a strong economy - 2003-07 delivered a seven-fold Sensex rise amid steady hikes.
Markets fear the pace and motive of rate rises (withdrawal of support) more than the level.
Low rates push spending and asset prices up; hikes redirect money to deposits and cool demand.
Every macro fact has two valid readings - position size for being wrong, not conviction for being right.

title_clean: US Rate Hikes and the Taper Tantrum Template
summary: QE and taper mechanics: post-2008 and post-2020 Fed bond-buying injected liquidity that flowed into emerging markets; the 2013 taper announcement sent Nifty down ~20% (6,200 to ~5,100). Feb-2021's yield spike re-ignited those fears as the US economy recovered. Speculator etymology as vigilance lesson.
lessons: Tapering withdraws the exact liquidity that inflated emerging markets - the 2013 Nifty −20% template.
Rates rising from growth are benign; rates rising from withdrawal of support are the danger.
Long-term investors can ignore tantrums; traders must respect them.
A speculator is literally a watchman on the border - vigilance is the job description.

title_clean: SEBI Peak Margin Rules: The Seller Squeeze and Structural VIX
summary: Peak margin (~15% on index futures vs ~5% international norm) ended broker intraday limits, forcing idle buffer cash and smaller positions. Fewer sellers meant richer premiums and a structurally higher India VIX. Proposes income thresholds or proficiency exams instead; cobra-effect parables for regulators.
lessons: Peak margin removed broker-funded intraday limits, so hedging legs need pre-funded buffer cash.
Fewer option sellers plus same buyers = higher premiums = structurally higher India VIX after the rules.
Margin hikes penalize the knowledgeable alongside the naive; access filters (income, exams) target risk directly.
Regulators risk the cobra effect: good intentions breeding the opposite outcome.

title_clean: Should You Buy Gold in 2021? The Three-Input Price Function
summary: Vindication of an Aug-2020 'gold peaked' call: gold below $1,700 vs Bank of America's $3,000/18-month forecast. Gold's Indian price = international price × USDINR × import duty. 2013-21 jewellery gold (~₹3,000 to ~₹4,500/g) underperformed bank FDs; duty cut 12.5% to 10% in Budget 2021.
lessons: Indian gold price decomposes into international price × USDINR × import duty - all three must align to rally.
From 2013 to 2021 jewellery gold returned ~50%, less than a bank FD - hedge, not compounding asset.
Gold hedges inflation and currency risk; with a stable rupee and rising rates expected, the hedge was cheap to skip.
Higher duty widens the smuggling arbitrage; the 2021 cut to 10% narrowed it.

title_clean: Q&A: Process Over Product, Cross-Hedging, IV vs VIX, Income Stocks
summary: Q&A batch: no-goals/process philosophy; cyclical-defensive and growth-value bull-bear mapping; cross-hedging equities with gold; implied volatility (individual) vs VIX (collective); ITC as dividend-plus-covered-call income (12-13% p.a.); valuation beats sector prediction; embracing uncertainty.
lessons: Process is more important than the product - outcomes are noise, method is signal.
Bull markets favour growth and cyclicals; bears favour defensives - but exceptions (2008-14 pharma) are common.
Implied volatility is per-stock or per-contract; VIX is the index-level aggregate of expectations.
Dividend yield plus covered-call writing can stack to low-double-digit returns on sleepy large caps.
Buy a bad business at a good price rather than a good business at a bad price.

title_clean: Q&A: The Correction-Waiting Trap, IV Crush, and Owning Your Losses
summary: Q&A: 'waiting for the big correction' guarantees never investing (Nifty 12,400→7,500→15,000 arc); Maruti's call premium fell despite the stock rising because event-IV crushed after auto-sales data; retail gains conviction only at tops; why crowdfunding trading losses is morally wrong; Reliance re-rating thesis; short covering vs long unwinding in one line.
lessons: Waiting for the big correction means never investing: enter when you have money, exit when you need it.
Event IV inflates option prices pre-data and crushes after - right direction can still lose to volatility value.
Retail conviction peaks at market tops and bottoms out at market lows - the crowd is a contrarian map.
Trading losses are the trader's responsibility; expecting crowdfunding is greed dressed as need.
Option value = price value + time value + volatility value - ignore the third at your peril.
